spots.name: Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site
spots.wiki: Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site
spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site), the reserve itself; Wikivoyage listing -38.675561,178.025278 agrees
spots.bio: A National Historic Reserve at the river mouth with the Cook monument, marking where Captain Cook first landed in New Zealand in 1769.
spots.reason: Inside Gisborne (about 1.5 km from the centre) and reached from the city. Skeptic notes it leans review but has two counted sources (Wikivoyage, DOC).

spots.name: Eastwoodhill Arboretum
spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (Eastwoodhill Arboretum); Wikivoyage listing -38.5625,177.7182 agrees within 300 m
spots.bio: New Zealand's largest planting of North American trees, 35 km north-west of Gisborne, with walks that are at their best in autumn.
spots.reason: About 26 km from Gisborne's centre (inside 75% of the 60 km span) and visited as a day trip from the city.

spots.name: Rere Rock Slide
spots.coordinates_source: OSM node 'Rere Falls & Rockslides' (the slide, not the falls at -38.5374,177.6096), as found by the skeptic
spots.bio: A natural rock slide where a stream runs over sloping rock into a pool, ridden on body boards or tyres, near the Rere Falls.
spots.reason: About 40 km from Gisborne's centre (just inside 75% of the span), reached from the city as a day trip. Its Wikipedia name redirects to the village of Rere, so views count as 0. wiki is 'Rere Falls' per the candidate; check the title in research.

spots.name: Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve), as found by the skeptic
spots.bio: A scenic reserve on SH2 with hot springs and pools at its entrance and walks through coastal forest and nīkau palms.

photo.file: Nikau Pools, Morere Hot Springs Reserve.jpg

spots.reason: About 40 km from Gisborne's centre (inside 75% of the span), on SH2 between Gisborne and Wairoa; Gisborne is the base most visitors drive from, and the point also lies within reach of Wairoa, which is not a destination. Two counted sources (DOC, Wikivoyage).

spots.name: Young Nick's Head
spots.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (natural=peninsula, Wikipedia link), as found by the skeptic
spots.bio: A headland south of Gisborne, the first land sighted by Cook's expedition in 1769, marked by a monument.
spots.reason: About 12 km from Gisborne's centre and a drive from the city.
needs_research: coordinates (confirm the car park or walk start, OSM point is the headland)

spots.name: Waikanae Beach
spots.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (Nominatim), as found by the skeptic; confirm OSM natural=beach
spots.bio: Gisborne's city swimming and surf beach, a 10 to 15 minute walk from the centre, running on into Midway Beach.
spots.reason: In the city. Photo: the only wide Commons file is a sunrise over the sea with no beach visible; the rest are the Cook statue. Needs a non-Commons photo (IMAGES.md), so the spot is held, not applied. No Wikipedia article of its own (the 'Waikanae' redirect is the Kāpiti Coast place), so confirm the OSM natural=beach feature.

spots.name: Anaura Bay
spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (Anaura Bay); this is a bay-area point, not yet the beach or campsite visit point the skeptic asked for
spots.bio: A beach and DOC campsite off SH35 north of Tolaga Bay, where Cook landed to take on water in 1769, with a coastal walkway.
spots.reason: About 54 km from Gisborne's centre, outside 75% of its 60 km span, so not Gisborne's; about 63 km from East Cape's centre, inside its 150 km span, and on the East Cape coast route with Tokomaru Bay and Cooks Cove.
needs_research: coordinates (beach or campsite visit point from DOC or OSM natural=beach)

spots.name: Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk
spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk): a point on the track, not a trailhead
spots.bio: A 46 km, three to four day Great Walk around Lake Waikaremoana, with huts to book ahead through DOC.

photo.file: New Zealand, Great Walk Lake Waikaremoana (43).JPG

spots.reason: Within about 6 km of Te Urewera's centre and reached from its Waikaremoana base. Distinct from the existing Lake Waikaremoana spot (te-urewera-1): that is the lake, this is the multi-day track.
needs_research: coordinates (Hopuruahine or Onepoto trailhead from DOC)

spots.name: Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park
spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (park centroid); the visit point (Minginui or the Whirinaki Waterfall track car park) still to be found
spots.bio: A conservation park of podocarp forest with tracks and huts on the Bay of Plenty and Hawke's Bay border.
spots.reason: About 41 km from Te Urewera's centre and reached from Murupara and Minginui on the Rotorua and Taupō side, not from Waikaremoana; over 50 km from Rotorua and 80 km from Whakatāne, so no destination surrounds it. Its Whirinaki Waterfall loop was rejected as part of this park. On the Bay of Plenty border, so the Bay of Plenty pass should not duplicate it.
needs_research: coordinates (Minginui or Whirinaki Waterfall car park)

spots.name: Wairoa
spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (Wairoa town); Wikivoyage -39.0333,177.3667 is the town page's point
spots.bio: The river town on the Wairoa River, the gateway to Lake Waikaremoana and the Māhia Peninsula.
spots.reason: About 46 km from the Māhia Peninsula and 40 km from Mōrere, the nearest other kept places, with only two kept places around it (every Wairoa sight was rejected), too few for a destination. About 100 km from Gisborne by road and outside every destination span.  Kept as a gateway town; Pipeline C sets its category and confirms the bio.
needs_research: bio check (town page lists no See item kept)

spots.name: Māhia Peninsula
spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (Māhia Peninsula): a peninsula centroid; the visit point (e.g. Māhia Beach) still to be found
spots.bio: A peninsula between Wairoa and Gisborne with beaches, scenic reserves and the Portland Island lighthouse.
spots.reason: Over 70 km from Gisborne's centre, outside Gisborne's span, and reached on its own via Nūhaka. No destination surrounds it.
needs_research: coordinates (visit point such as Māhia Beach)
